The first pathway links Tiapride to 6-phosphofructo-2-kinase/fructose-2,6-bisphosphatase 4, which is then targeted by a compound with a known mechanism of action. This compound, in turn, targets Solute carrier organic anion transporter family member 1B1, indicating a potential role in the transport of organic anions. The second pathway connects Tiapride to Valacyclovir hydrolase, which is targeted by (+)-Pseudodeflectusin, a compound that also targets Solute carrier organic anion transporter family member 1B1. The third pathway links Tiapride to Inosine-5'-monophosphate dehydrogenase 2, which is targeted by a complex molecule that ultimately targets the same transporter. These findings suggest that Tiapride may influence the activity of Solute carrier organic anion transporter family member 1B1 through different molecular mechanisms, possibly involving enzyme inhibition or modulation of transport processes. The integrated evidence supports a potential role for Tiapride in modulating the activity of this transporter, though the exact mechanism remains to be fully elucidated.
